text:
For the first time since Halloween, the Maple Leafs won a hockey game. They had to come from two goals down on Long Island to do it, and the goal that flipped it came from the rookie whose handling has become its own subplot of their November.

The skid was nine games (0-8-1), long enough that the headlines had moved past the standings to Auston Matthews' future, with one quoting his own words, "We should be embarrassed," and Elliotte Friedman saying "All bets are off." Jim Hiller's treatment of Gavin McKenna drew public criticism from Bruce Boudreau. Down 2-0 after Anthony Duclair scored early and Mathew Barzal added one in the second, Toronto's chances of ending it looked thin.

But the Leafs had been the better team from the second period on, and the chances finally turned into goals. Dakota Joshua deflected one home at 10:14 of the second. Chris Tanev, whose load management has been a story of its own, tied it 3:52 into the third off a Matthews feed. Then McKenna, on a delayed penalty, pounced on a rebound at 8:55 after Ilya Sorokin stopped a blast. That goal moved Toronto's win chance from 48% to 79%. Easton Cowan added an empty-netter after Sorokin went to the bench with 2:11 left.

The process backs the result. Toronto took 66% in deserved to win, out-chanced the Islanders 2.88 to 1.75 in expected goals and allowed just 0.20 in the third. Darren Raddysh had two assists and seven shots; he and Jake McCabe set up both Joshua's goal and McKenna's. Anthony Stolarz's best stop came on Bo Horvat in the third with the game tied.

One win does not settle anything Matthews or Hiller has been asked about this month. It does end the wait, and McKenna, in 12:48 of ice time, was named first star.

The Islanders also lost Kyle Palmieri to a lower-body injury, per Daily Faceoff, a worry on top of the loss.
headline: Leafs end nine-game skid with third-period comeback
